source.title: Learning Rate Matters: Vanilla LoRA May Suffice for LLM Fine-tuning
source.authors: Yu-Ang Lee; Ching-Yun Ko; Pin-Yu Chen; M. Yeh

record.file_problem: Full paper text is provided; no apparent truncation or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests LoRA fine-tuning methods and learning-rate sensitivity on pretrained decoder-only LLMs, not the claim's random-initialization training of large non-convex networks or the CIFAR training-error outcomes. The relevant relationships are only adjacent to the listed versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports downstream benchmark accuracy, method comparisons, and Hessian measurements. These do not measure training classification error from random initialization, bad local minima in teacher-student ReLU networks, plain-network depth, or training recovery above a stability limit. Cited results about other studies are not extracted as this study's results.
record.test_reason: The study measures downstream accuracy after LoRA fine-tuning and block-wise Hessian eigenvalues at initialization. It does not measure any version's specified training behavior. Initialization comparisons do not test activation-matched signal propagation or trainable depth (V4); learning-rate sweeps and initial curvature do not establish recovery above a stability threshold or edge-of-stability dynamics (V5).
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: after method-specific learning-rate tuning, the tested LoRA methods generally achieve comparable downstream performance; marginal advantages depend on rank and setting. The authors also associate differing preferred learning-rate ranges with initial Hessian curvature and recommend more comprehensive tuning.
record.recipe_differences: The study fine-tunes pretrained LLMs using LoRA and related parameter-efficient methods, rather than training large networks from random initialization as in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported downstream performance and preferred learning-rate ranges vary with method, learning rate, batch size, rank, training duration, model, and task. These settings do not measure the outcomes named by the claim versions.

fits_no_version.finding: Method-specific learning-rate tuning yields broadly comparable downstream accuracy across the tested LoRA methods, with small, rank-dependent differences (Sections 3.3 and A).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The tested LoRA variants generally achieve similar peak downstream accuracy when their learning rates are tuned separately.

fits_no_version.finding: LoRA initialization variants have different initial block-wise Hessian eigenvalues, generally inversely associated with their preferred learning-rate ranges (Section 4.2; Appendix I). These measurements provide neither training trajectories nor a full-model stability threshold.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Initial adapter curvature can help indicate relative learning-rate ranges for LoRA fine-tuning.

record.problems: The paper's reported metrics are downstream benchmark accuracy and Hessian estimates, not training classification error. Llama experiments are not reported with three-run means and standard deviations, unlike the other experiments. Several additional results are presented in figures, and not all plotted values are numerically transcribed in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No results meet the row criteria for the specified claim versions: the study's own outcomes are LoRA downstream benchmark performance and Hessian analysis, not the behaviors those versions name. Cited findings from prior work are not rows.

untested.parts: Training classification error of randomly initialized convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/100, including corrupted labels and model-size or regularization effects.
Spurious local minima and the effect of extra student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Depth-dependent training degradation, prevention by identity shortcuts, and the specified initialization or normalization exceptions.
Activation-matched initialization preserving signals and gradients, training speed and trainable depth, and orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization in the specified plain networks.
Loss recovery above the initial stability limit, accompanying curvature reduction, full-batch edge-of-stability dynamics, and divergence relative to that threshold.
Batch normalization's effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and comparable training with Fixup without normalization.

record.verdict_notes: Correct the record's relation from tests to discusses; retain T6. The paper discusses V5's original catapult and edge-of-stability findings and uses Kaiming initialization, but supplies no results testing those versions. The empty result-row set is appropriate, and rows_left_out already declares the excluded outcomes.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error, random initialization of the full network, CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, and effects of model size or early stopping.
Teacher-student two-layer ReLU local minima, initialization from standard random weights, and student width relative to teacher width.
Plain versus residual network training error as depth changes; special initialization for very deep plain networks; residual training without normalization.
Activation-matched initialization, signal or gradient propagation, trainable depth, tanh networks, and orthogonal convolutional kernels.
Training above a stability limit, transient loss increases and recovery, edge-of-stability sharpness dynamics, and divergence rates under those conditions.
Batch normalization effects on training speed or learning-rate tolerance in the named model and dataset settings; Fixup training without normalization.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
